To whom it may concern:
This letter is in regard to the Show Low Mountain Ranch Proposed Amended Master Development Plan, 
MDP-A 23-001. This letter is a joint representation of neighbors living near the proposed plan and will 
include our thoughts and concerns of the new development. Names and address of those represented 
here will be included below. We would like to thank you for letting us voice our concerns and thoughts 
to you this day. 
The presentation that was given on Thursday, September 21, 2023, at the Navajo County Public Works 
Planning and Zoning meeting was well received. However, many of our neighbors did not receive a 
notice about the hearing, or the notice was sent out just a few short days before the meeting and some 
of us were out of town and could not make it back in time to be present at the meeting, whether it be in 
person or through Zoom, to pose any questions or concerns regarding the proposed plan. Below is a list 
of our concerns, in no particular order.
1. Traffic – Bourdon Ranch Road is already congested. We have had several accidents in our area 
with some being fatal. With 700+ new structures/lots, we fear this will only increase the already 
existing problem.
2. Water – How will so many new structures affect our water supply. Will there be a concern of 
this in the future. Will we end up like North Scottsdale and run out of water?
3. Sewer – We don’t have concerns about the sewer lines, as we are on a septic system. However, 
will White Mountain Lake be able to handle the onslaught of all these new dwellings?
4. Lights – Sitting out and staring off into the night sky is a pastime enjoyed by many. That is one of 
the joys of living out in the country. Will the new development have streetlights or are they 
going to preserve our view of the night sky?
5. Will the new development have an HOA or CC&R’s? We understand that most of the homes will 
be manufactured homes, park models, or recreational vehicles. We don’t have a problem with 
that, as most of our homes are manufactured homes. We do have a problem with people who 
let their homes become run down. We don’t want a trailer park that overtime becomes 
rundown with abandoned or junked out trailers. 
6. Most of us on Roundup Drive have farm animals. We know all too well that when new 
communities come in a lot of those new folks start complaining about their new neighbors, us. 
We don’t want to start having complaints thrown at us. Not one person on our road complains 
about what the other person has. Some of us have dogs, cats, horses, donkeys, goats, peacocks, 
geese, chickens, etc. Sometimes those animal noises carry across the land. WE DON’T WANT 
COMPLAINTS and we’re not going to stop raising what we have. How will this be handled by the 
new development? Not meaning to sound rude but we are concerned.

<!-- page 1069 -->
7. We want to make sure that there will be no access to the property using Roundup Drive. That 
the gate mentioned will be in place and locked, and that the only time it will be used is in the 
case of an emergency. 
8. Why so many new structures/lots/spaces? Is there any way to increase the lots sizes so there 
are not so many new dwellings in a small area? Can we preserve the area and not become what 
Prescott or Flagstaff have become?
9. How will this affect first responders? They’re pushed to the limits already in our area.
Thank you,

adopted by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors in 2007 through Resolution 96-07 and allowed for 
the 307 acres of subject parcels to be developed out to a maximum of 508 units.  
 
There is currently a water tank and water lines already partially installed, and the sewer has been at least 
partially tied in to the first phase of the development with a lift station having been installed and a valve 
for pressure having been attempted to be installed.  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission  unanimously recommended approval of this 
Master Development Plan Amendment request to the Board of Supervisors at the September 21st, 2023, 
meeting, to include all conditions put forth by Staff.

with the request that the applicant hold a community meeting so as to hear concerns from neighbors 
within the vicinity of the project.

Community Association Building/Post Office.  Notice of this meeting was overnighted by the applicant

• Fencing off of grazing cattle and grazing cattle being on the property.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
This project is designed to contain the following components: 
 
• Area A (designated as Parcel “A” within the proposal): Commercial district along the west side 
of Bourdon Ranch Road, approximately 6.8 acres  
o In addition to the commercial uses that have already been approved, this request seeks 
the addition for self-storage use(s), including outdoor RV, boat and/or vehicle (outdoor) 
storage. 
o The commercial district along the east side of Bourdon Ranch Road (~9.5 acres) is to 
remain unchanged and is not a part of this Amendment request. 
• Area B (designated as Parcel “B” within the proposal): Recreational Vehicle/Park Model Resort, 
approximately 178.2 acres.  
o This portion of the development would allow for the development of up to 350 
Recreational Vehicle/Park Model spaces/lots consisting of one or more Recreational 
Vehicle/Park Model Park(s), with individual spaces under common ownership, and/or 
Recreational Vehicle/Park Model Subdivision(s), with individually platted and owned 
Recreational Vehicle/Park Model lots. Portions/phases of this area may be age-restricted 
(55+). Included within Parcel “B” are various amenities in support of the proposed 
phase(s).  
o Also proposed within Area B is the ability to allow for outdoor storage of recreational 
vehicles. 
• Area C (designated as Parcel “C” within the proposal): Cottage Community, approximately 32.4 
acres.  
o Allow for the development of approximately 96 spots/lots for Recreational Vehicle/Park 
Model Park(s) within a more intimate “cottage”- or cluster-type arrangement as indicated 
on the Overall Design & Conceptual Site Plan Amended Master Development Plan also 
included with the submittal. This may be developed as either individual spaces under 
common ownership ( i.e., “Park”) and/or as a Subdivision(s) with individually platted 
and owned Recreational Vehicle/Park Model lots. Portions/phases of this Parcel may be 
age-restricted (55+).  
o Also included within this area are various amenities in support of Park as well as the 
ability to allow for outdoor storage. 
• Area D (designated as Parcel “D” within the proposal): Manufactured Home/Recreational 
Vehicle Community, approximately 80.0 acres 
o Allow for the development of up to 312 lots/spaces for one or more Manufactured Home 
(“MH”) and/or Recreational Vehicle Community(s) as either/both a “Park” with 
individual spaces under common ownership and/or Subdivision(s) with individually

<!-- page 1076 -->
Board of Supervisors              5 | P a g e  
 
platted and owned lots. Park models may be included in any given phase or portion  of 
Area D.  
o Included within this area are various amenities in support of the proposed use, along with 
the possibility for outdoor storage. 
 
ZONING DISTRICT: 
ARTICLE  17 – (SD) – SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT ZONE 
 
Section 1701 – Purpose  
 
1. The purpose of the Special Development zone is to provide for the development of subdivisions and other 
land use projects containing various dwelling types, necessary commercial centers, off street parking areas, 
open space areas for recreation, and to preserve a rural atmosphere.  
2. Deviations from design standards for the specific zone or zones may be permitted provided open spaces are 
developed and maintained for the use of the residents and provided further that the parcel size, soil conditions, 
terrain, ground cover and other significant natural features favor this type of development. 
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN/AREA PLAN:  
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Land Use Element 
 
Goal 4:  Provide equal opportunity for safe, decent, sanitary, and affordable housing for all 
residents of the County and provide a range of residential uses that offer housing opportunities 
for all County residents. 
 
Policy 4-B: Promote greater flexibility and economy of land use, provide opportunities in the 
Zoning Ordinance for alternative housing types and patterns, planned developments, mixed uses, 
and other innovations that reduce development costs. 
• The proposed amendments expand the scope of the Show Low Mountain Ranch 
development to include a higher number of lots/spaces, as well as add additional mixed 
uses to the project – effectively providing for more housing type options for the 
community.  
 
Policy 4-D: Consider developing standards for development density that reflect the needs and 
goals of existing communities, whether incorporated or unincorporated, e.g., medium to high-
density residential zoning for Community Villages and Rural Edge areas and low to medium -
density for developing rural areas. 
• The mixed uses included in the proposal expand the utilization of the land to appeal to 
the needs of the area and align with the Community Village character area of White 
Mountain Lake.  
 
Goal 6: Maintain compatible land use patterns while encouraging free market development. 
 
Policy 6 -A: Encourage the use of, and provide incentives such as density bonuses for,

<!-- page 1077 -->
Board of Supervisors              6 | P a g e  
 
implementation of community master plans. 
• The proposed amendments to the Master Development Plan for the Show Low Mountain 
Ranch development encourage the project to continue.  
 
Policy 6-B: Consider, if needed, providing for buffers between different land uses including, but 
not limited to, setbacks, walls or fences, and landscaping.  
• The proposal includes landscaping, complete with a walking/bicycling trail, to provide 
a buffer between the development and the surrounding areas.  
 
Policy 6-C:  Require paved or other appro priately surfaced access to commercial or industrial 
uses.  
• The proposal includes paved access to the commercial district located at the east of the 
development.  
 
Goal 7:  Facilitate commercial and industrial development, including business and technology 
uses, where appropriate, to increase employment opportunities. 
 
Policy 7 -A: Encourage strategic placement of commercial development so as to attract and 
locate shopping and employment uses that have paved or other appropriately surfaced access 
and are easily accessible, particularly in or near established communities a nd cities, and in 
communities with air and/or rail access. 
• The proposed amendments retain the previously approved commercial district and  
expand the allowed uses in the commercial district to include a larger range of 
commercial ventures.  
 
Goal 8: Reduce the danger from fire for all residents living in a wildland urban interface or near 
a National Forest boundary. 
 
Policy 8 -C: Discourage high -density development in areas where fire protection and other 
emergency services are not readily available. 
• The development is within a distance from emergency services that Staff has determined 
to be reasonable for the proposed density of the development.  
 
Policy 8-D: Continue to require multiple access routes into new large subdivisions and other 
major developments for emergency purposes and to improve traffic circulation pursuant to the 
Subdivision Regulations & Requirements. 
• The proposed amendments include primary access to the development from Bourdon 
Ranch Road and secondary access to Bourdon Ranch Road from a connection between 
the development and the existing Roundup Road to the south of the subject site. 
 
Policy 8 -E: Continue the review by the Fire Districts in the approval of subdivisions and 
development projects within their respective jurisdictions. 
• The Fire District under which their jurisdiction falls has reviewed the proposal and has 
provided feedback to the applicant and Staff.  
 
Goal 9: Actively plan to accommodate growth in Navajo County in an appropriate manner. 
 
Policy 9-B: Encourage higher density and intensity development in those areas of the County

<!-- page 1078 -->
Board of Supervisors              7 | P a g e  
 
where services, including water and sewer systems, paved rights -of-way, and schools, are 
available or can be created with new development. 
• The Community Village character area of White Mountain Lake provides ample 
opportunity for growth, in-line with the development of the proposal.  
 
Policy 9-D: Encourage in-fill opportunities in the County to capitalize on existing infrastructure 
and reduce growth-related costs. 
• The proposed amendments to the Show Low Mountain Ranch development serve to 
uphold the previous intention to complete the development, and further uphold the 
opportunity to utilize the pre-existing infrastructure.  
 
Circulation Element 
 
Goal 1: Provide a range of circulation options that are safe and efficient and that complement 
local communities and the natural environment.  
 
Policy 1 -B: Coordinate land use and circulation planning to encourage comprehensive and 
efficient development and growth patterns that support adjacent land uses, complement the 
character of adjacent communities and neighborhoods, and mitigate impacts on the natural 
environment. 
• The proposed access points utilize existing and, in the case of Bourdon Ranch Road, 
larger roadways. Additionally, the proposed circulatory roadways within the 
development are complimentary to the surrounding neighborhood roadways.  
 
Goal 4: Provide for safe travel and access to property.  
 
Policy 4-B: Continue working with developers and property owners to achieve safe and legal 
access for all properties.  
• All proposed access points to the development have been determined to be safe and legal.  
 
Policy 4-E: Include consideration of, and planning for, pedestrian, equestrian, handicapped -
accessibility and bicycle use when designing circulation infrastructure improvements through 
addition of trails, sidewalks, signage, pavement markings, or other treatments. 
• The proposed amendments include a walking/bicycling trail through the southern open-
space landscaping of the development.  
 
Character Area 
 
The purpose of the Community Village character area is to provide large areas with higher density 
residential development with a mix of related commercial, industrial, and institutional uses extending 
from highway corridors and highway intersections. Community Village is an appropriate and 
encouraged location for uses such as community college campuses and hospitals or medical clinics. 
 
Analysis: 
 
The proposed Master Development Plan Amendment meets all relevant goals and policies of the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance and the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan as described above.

<!-- page 1079 -->
Board of Supervisors              8 | P a g e  
 
 
Planning and Development Services Staff have  received three public comments in opposition of the 
project as of October 10th, 2023. The concerns raised within the two letters  and one voicemail pertain 
to: 
• Traffic – specifically regarding congestion on Bourdon Ranch Road. 
• Water – assurance of supply. 
• Sewer – ability to support new tie-ins of that quantity. 
• Lighting – night sky preservation.  
• HOA or CCRs – prevention of unsightly code violations. 
• Farm animals – prevention of revocation of animal stewardship  
• Access – emergency-only access to Roundup. 
• Density – increase lot/space sizes to decrease quantity of lots/spaces. 
• Usage – area appropriateness for short-term residency.   
• Emergency Response – ability of first responders to serve project.  
• Drainage – parcel is typically muddy. 
• Cell reception – lack of service with current service load. 
• Internet – lack of current services in area.  
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The item has been properly noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised Statutes 
and Article 29.  
 
This item was posted in the October 4th, 2023, edition of the Holbrook Tribune.  Postcards were 
mailed to neighbors within 300 feet of the property. The property was  posted with public hearing 
notices.  
 
2. The proposal is in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
 
The proposed amendments meet several applicable goals within Navajo County’s Comprehensive 
Plan, as noted within this report. 
 
3. The proposed amendments are compatible with the permissible uses in the zoning district in 
which the property is located. 
 
The proposed amendments are compatible with permissible uses within the Special Development 
zoning district, as proposed. 
 
4. The proposed amendments are compatible with the current and likely future uses of 
properties in the vicinity of the development.  
 
The proposed amendments have been determined to be compatible with current and likely future 
uses per the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance.  
 
5. The proposed amendments will have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and 
general welfare of properties in the vicinity of the development.

Given the nature of the property and the zoning of the ne ighborhood, there should be minimal

PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT SERVICES RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo  County Planning and Development Services Staff recommend approval of the Master 
Development Plan Amendment, subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. All Federal, State, and Navajo County permits required for each lot must be obtained and adhered to. 
 
2. This Master Development Site Plan shall allow for a maximum of 758 residential units. 
 
3. A Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA), Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, Sanitary Sewer Collection 
System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report for the development, prepared by a 
Professional Engineer, licensed in the State of Arizona, shall be submitted to and approved by the 
County Engineer’s office before the T entative Plat and/or Site Plan Review is submitted to the 
Planning and Zoning Commission.   
 
4. All required offsite improvements identified in the TIA, Master Drainage Plan, Floodplain Study, 
Sanitary Sewer Collection System Design Report, and Water Distribution Design Report shall be 
constructed or financially assured before the stage of development is constructed that requires the 
improvement.  On-site sanitary systems, such as septic systems, shall not be allowed as an alternative 
to a Sanitary Sewer Collection System. 
 
5. Sufficient off-road drainage easements shall be made available to accommodate drainage, up to a 100-
year event, as required. 
 
6. Drainage structures, including detention or retention ponds, shall be designed to accommodate a 100-
year event and shall be proposed with the Final Plat and/or Site Plan Review, as required. 
 
7. Access connecting to Roundup Drive shall provide emergency access only. Crash gates shall be 
installed. Roundup Drive and the connecting roadways shall not be used by construction vehicles or 
equipment.

<!-- page 1081 -->
Board of Supervisors              10 | P a g e  
 
 
8. Any commercial development within the area indicated as Parcel A shall require Site Plan Review 
approval from the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission prior to development.  
 
9. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations shall be met before approval of the Tentative 
Plat and/or Site Plan Review. Variances shall be requested in accordance with Section 4.12. 
 
10. All technical requirements of the Subdivision Regulations and Requirements, Flood Control 
Ordinance, Building Safety Ordinance, and applicable codes shall be adhered to and approved at the 
proper Tentative Plat, Final, or Building Permit and construction phase (to include, without limitation, 
the Traffic Impact Analysis, Drainage Study, Floodplain Study, Construction Improvement Plans, and 
Grading Plans). 
 
11. Approval of the Master Development Site Plan is conditioned upon the submittal for a request for 
either a Tentative Plat or for a Site Plan Review to the Planning and Zoning Commission, along with 
proof of compliance with the above conditions, within 24 months of the date of Board of Supervisors 
Resolution. If this condition is not met, approval shall be revoked, and the Master Development Site 
Plan shall become null and void. This condition shall be conclusively deemed to have been satisfied 
unless the Board of Supervisors causes a notice of revocation to be recorded in the Office of the Navajo 
County Recorder within 30 days after the expiration of the 24-month period (or any extension thereof).

Date 
03.18.2023 
 
Our house rules are designed to maintain a peaceful and considerate living space 
for all tenants as well as contribute to the maintenance of long-term sobriety.. 
Rules may only be changed following a house meeting and unanimous vote with 
staff present and wherein the change strengthens and pro motes the well-being of 
everyone residing and Step Inn as a whole. 
  House Rules 
 No drugs or alcohol on the property; this includes medical 
marijuana.  
 No persons under the influence or that appear under the influence 
are permitted on property. 
 Visitors are not permitted unless part of a fellowship providing 
service.  
 Curfew is 10 PM unless otherwise necessary due to employment and 
approved by on duty House Manager. A copy of your work schedule 
will be required and kept on file. 
 Quiet hours are observed from 8 PM until 8 AM to respect various 
schedules.     
 Laundry is to be done during off peak hours when possible. The 
laundry schedule is to be followed and tenants will only utilize 
their allotted laundry time/day. 
 Bathroom schedules may be adapted if necessary. 
 Dress codes are enforced. No clothes should display drugs, 
alcohol or paraphernalia.  
 Smoking is permitted outside ONLY this includes vapes and e-
cigarettes.

Notice of Intent 
Step Inn, LLC 
3077 Browning Ln. Lakeside, AZ 85929 
Tel: 928.245.2940 
Email: sburnett@mystepinn.com 
  
  
Sept 25, 2023 
   
Dear Neighbor, 
  
I am writing to notify you of my intent to establish a residential behavioral health facility. The 
facility will be at my residence, located at 3077 Browning Ln., Lakeside, AZ 85929.  
 
If approved, the main structure, as well as an addition, will be used to facilitate and house a 
maximum of 7 individuals and 2 staff. Structures and staff adhere to all State licensing 
requirements and regulations to ensure the safety of clients and the public. 
The main purpose of Step Inn is to provide unmeet housing and recovery needs of clients 
currently in and/or having recently completed Inpatient and Outpatient treatment programs. 
Unlike traditional treatment centers, Step Inn homes will safely facilitate real life exposure and 
aid in navigating the challenges presented during and post treatment. Treatment centers are 
great for arresting the disease of addiction; however, elements of daily life situations and 
obstacles cannot be experienced within the confines of treatment. We firmly believe intensive 
transitional living is the crucial piece missing in the treatment process and this lack is ultimately 
responsible for the high recidivism rates for relapse. It is our sole purpose to provide healthy 
living environments and provide services to help clients apply treatment tools and navigate life 
in a new healthy way. Step Inn staff is comprised of experienced and credentialed professionals 
to demonstrate their success in maintaining a healthy, clean and sober lifestyle. Their lived 
experiences have a unique advantage to help others adapt outside of treatment centers. Our 
peer approach is proven to be most successful in other leading recovery homes. Also, Step Inn 
will require clients to be actively involved in 12-step programs which have the highest success 
rates worldwide to date. Step Inn homes will remain small quaint home settings to keep their 
sole purpose intact and aligned with its mission to replicate ordinary life and building 
foundations for realistic long-term recovery. 
 I enjoy the community where I live and therefore have policies in place to uphold a strong 
vetting system to ensure likely candidates for success and preserve the neighborhood 
dynamics. This home will be considered long-term housing in that more than 6 months may be 
utilized however, my intention is to assist clients in becoming self-sufficient and obtaining 
permanent residences of their own within a 6 month stay.  
The services will include 12-step application, individual and group therapy; cognitive behavior 
interventions; behavioral therapy; and employment services. All services will be provided by 
qualified licensed professionals in person as well as via zoom. The facility will work closely with 
the Arizona Department of Health Services and other health care and social service providers.

<!-- page 1138 -->
Possible Concerns: 
1. Traffic – We do not anticipate added traffic with the exception of one company vehicle 
to provide transportation to tenants. Step Inn will not be a location frequented by the 
public. Tenant visitors are not permitted at the home. 
2. Parking- The 40’ x 20’ existing parking lot is plentiful for the operation of the company, 
there are 5 parking spaces. 
3. Roadway- The existing roadway is adequate for travel.  
4. Accessibility- Step Inn will provide special need accessibility to the extent that it does 
not require medical attention as we are not pursuing licensing which permits the care of 
individuals with medical disability. Step Inn is a non-medical facility.    
5. Utilities- The residence is currently on county water and sewage, with ample electrical 
output.  
6. Privacy – Barriers and landscape buffers around the property will ensure privacy not 
only for tenants but also for neighboring houses. Stringent vetting systems, curfews, 
house rules and staff supervision will also ensure privacy. Step Inn enforces the Good 
Neighbor policy required for this type of operation. Please see attached policies I and 
XVII.  
 
On March 17, 2023, Step Inn published a notice in the White Mountain Independent informing 
the public of its incorporation. A copy of the notice is attached.  
 
I look forward to hearing from you and answering any questions you may have.  
  
  
Sincerely,

Letter pertaining to Step Inn

I am composing this letter on behalf of Step Inn, located in the beautiful Lakeside, AZ.  
After more than 2 decades of therapeutic services in the White Mountains, it pleases me 
to put support in and with the owners of Step Inn.   
 
The concept of having a residential behavioral health home has been sorely needed in the 
mountains.  This house will help those individuals that need the transitional support from 
addiction to productive involvement back into society.  This is where there is such a large 
drop off when it comes to supporting recovering addicts.  Too many of these good people 
have so many challenges, when they quit using, that circumstances overpower them and 
leave them broken and beaten down.  Having a home like this will allow these individuals 
to have support while they build up to win against these challenges.  
 
Sarah Burnett is the perfect candidate for opening a home in this industry.  She has the 
energy and empathy to help people that are struggling.  She is also connected well to the 
recovery community and will have the connections and confidence to build the needed 
bridges for the people that choose to live in this home.   
 
Approving and supporting the concept of Step Inn will help the individual but will also 
help the community.  Having people that overcome and are productive is much more 
beneficial to the community than those that are burdening the community and court due 
to the challenges and poor choices of their life.

the high level direct interaction I have with Sarah multiple times in a day or week, I am confident in her ability and 
expertise in the operations and oversight of behavioral health facilities. I own a medical billing company and Sarah is 
employed by one of my clients. While typically I do not involve myself in writing such a letter as this, I find it imperative 
that the behavioral health field has an increase of integrity and leadership as I have directly seen with Sarah. 
The success rate of people surviving the disease of alcoholism and addiction is sadly quite low and there have been 
recent events of owners that have taken advantage of this vulnerable population. I personally have seen Sarah go above 
and beyond in multiple roles within a company that is not owned by her to ensure that the patients/clients have exactly 
what they need to recover. If you can imagine for a moment that you had a family member in need of behavioral health

and their owners have. 
Sarah demonstrates exemplary professionalism and ethics (and believe me when I tell you I have seen folks who do not).

everything Sarah does is well above board and with integrity.  
Sarah brings a unique attitude of ownership and accountability for organizational culture and purpose which contributes 
greatly to the success of treatment within the community. Sarah has also shown a deep compassion for the vulnerable 
population and stands up and fights for individuals in need of services and diligently ensures their wellbeing and 
equality.  
At the core of any successful treatment center is a purpose and team with shared vision. I have seen this dynamic 
firsthand in Sarah’s current position and do not doubt that she will do an excellent job of providing services within a 
residential program.  
The hybrid approach of Step Inn’s business model truly encompasses all levels of recovery from beginning to end

realistic, tangible and ingenious. Sarah’s business model has an advantage due to size and structure of treatment

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
Recommendation: The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission, as well as Planning and 
Development Staff recommends approval of the Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions of this 
Staff Report. 
 
Location: The property is located south of White Mountain Lakes; APN # 404-42-013B. 
 
Size: One (1) parcel totaling 8.00 acres.  
 
Supervisor District: III. 
 
Zoning: RU-1. 
 
Property Owners: Stanley G. and Carolyn M. Brewer. 
 
Applicant: Vertical Bridge.  
 
Representative: Todd Daoust.  
 
REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
Consideration of a request by Vertical Bridge for a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of 
a 95’ monopole communication tower and associated facilities in the White Mountain Lakes  area. 
APN#: 404-42-013B, T11N, R23E, S 31 of the GSRM. Owner: Stanley G. and Carolyn M. Brewer . 
Agent: Todd Daoust. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
The land in the vicinity of this project is zoned RU-1, with residences to the north and east, and vacant 
land to the south and west.

<!-- page 1180 -->
Board of Supervisors              2 | P a g e  
 
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
This proposal would allow for one (1) 95’ monopole wireless communication facility and associated 
facilities on a vacant, 8.00-acre lot. The proposal would be an appropriate usage within the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance, if approved for a Special Use Permit. 
 
On October 19 th, 2023, the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously 
recommended approval of the Special Use Permit for AZ3 Cochise Wireless Communication Facility.  
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The proposed project is a 95’ monopole wireless communication facility and its associated facilities. 
This tower will be located at least 100ft. away from all property lines on APN# 404-42-013B. The tower 
and all associated equipment will be located in a 100’x100’area and surrounded by an 8ft. chain-link 
fence.  
 
ZONING DISTRICT: 
ARTICLE  8 – (RURAL-1) – RURAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 401 – Purpose  
 
The principal purpose of this district is to conserve and protect open land uses, as well as foster orderly growth 
in rural areas, and prevent urban and agricultural land use conflicts. The primary purpose of requiring large 
minimum parcels of not less than one (1) acre in area is to discourage small lot or residential subdivisions 
where public facilities such as water, sewage disposal, parks and playgrounds, and governmental services such 
as police and fire protection are not available or could not reasonably be made currently available. principal 
uses permitted in this zoning district include both farm and non-farm residential uses, farms, and recreational 
and institutional uses. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
 34. Television, wireless towers, and radio transmitter towers and stations, subject  
 to approval by Federal Regulatory Agencies. 
 
Article 25 – General Provisions 
 
Section 2521 – Wireless Communication Facilities

<!-- page 1181 -->
Board of Supervisors              3 | P a g e  
 
The purpose of this Section is to establish rules and regulations for the siting of wireless 
communication facilities. The goals of this Section are to provide for the development of 
wireless communication services County-wide by:  
 
1. Considering public safety, health, and welfare.  
 
2. Considering impact on adjacent properties. 
 
3. Encouraging configuration which minimizes additional visual impact through proper 
siting, design, landscape, and camouflage techniques.  
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN/AREA PLAN:  
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Land Use Element 
 
Goal 6: Maintain compatible land use patterns while encouraging free market development. 
 
Policy 6-B: Consider, if needed, providing for buffers between different land uses including, but 
not limited to, setbacks, walls or fences, and landscaping.  
 
• The applicant has indicated they will setback their wireless communication tower a 
minimum of 100’ from all property lines, which exceeds the requirements of the Navajo 
County Zoning Ordinance or facilities of this nature. They have also indicated would be 
amenable to coating the tower to further assist with stealthing. Additionally, the applicant 
has indicated they will construct an 8ft. tall chain-link fence around the perimeter of the 
lease area, acting as a buffer between the proposed tower and existing  residences in the 
subject area.  
 
Goal 9: Actively plan to accommodate growth in Navajo County in an appropriate manner. 
 
Policy 9-F: Encourage development/installation of technology improvements including, but not 
limited to, high speed Internet lines and other communications improvements in Navajo County. 
 
• The applicant is proposing the addition of this wireless communication tower and 
associated facilities to provide higher quality wireless service for residents, businesses, 
visitors, and emergency services in this region of Navajo County. 
 
Analysis: 
 
The proposed special use meets all relevant goals and policies of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance 
and the Navajo County  Comprehensive Plan as described above. This project, and its submittal, meet 
all requirements of Section 2521 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance, which regulates wireless 
communication facilities.  
 
Planning and Development Services Staff have  received one comment in opposition, as well as one 
comment in favor of this project, as of November 7th, 2023.

<!-- page 1182 -->
Board of Supervisors              4 | P a g e  
 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The item has been properly noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised Statutes 
and Article 29.  
 
This item was posted in the October 25th, 2023, edition of the Holbrook Tribune.  Postcards were 
mailed to neighbors within 300 feet of the property. The property was posted with public hearing 
notices, in accordance with the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance and Arizona Revised Statutes.  
 
2. The proposal is in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
 
The proposed project meets a ll applicable goals within Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan, as 
noted within this report. 
 
3. The proposed use is compatible with the permissible uses in the zoning district in which the 
property is located. 
 
The proposed use is compatible with permissible uses within the RU-1 zoning district. 
 
4. The proposed use is  compatible with the current and likely future uses of properties in the 
vicinity of the proposed use.  
 
The proposed use has been determined to be compatible with current and likely future uses per the 
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance.  
 
5. The proposed use will have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general 
welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
 
Given the nature of the property and the zoning of the ne ighborhood, there should be minimal 
adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general welfare of properties in the vicinity of the 
proposed use.

The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission, as well as Navajo County Planning and Development 
Services Staff, recommend approval of the Special Use Permit, subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall permit 1 (one)  monopole wireless communication tower, not to 
exceed 95 feet in height, and accessory structures necessary for operation of the tower on the 
subject property. 
 
2. The applicant shall obtain a Building Permit from Navajo County for such tower and facilities 
prior to commencing construction. 
 
3. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning communication towers 
prior to any building permits being issued. 
 
4. The tower shall be constructed as a monopole, as indicated in the supplied plans.  The owner of 
the tower shall maintain the tower, antennae as necessary. 
 
5. A fence of material acceptable to the Planning and Development Services Director shall be constructed 
to enclose the base of the tower and necessary accessory structures.  
 
6. A Geotechnical Report for the Access Easement shall be submitted and approved. 
 
7. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan.  Any 
expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this permit. 
 
8. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period, from the date of 
Board approval, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
9. Should the operator decide to abandon the use of the tower, they shall notify Navajo County 
Planning and Development Services that the tower is no longer being utilized. 
 
10. If the tower is no longer being utilized, the property owner shall cause, at their expense, the 
removal of all components of this tower within a 90-day period. 
 
11. The owner shall provide reasonable cooperation to other public and private users who may be 
interested in collocation on this tower and shall consider such collocation upon commercially 
reasonable terms, unless such collocation is not technically feasible. 
 
12. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the specific use and 
to the specific property for which it is issued. Upon completion and final inspection by the Planning

the Special Use Permit shall thereafter be transferable and shall run with the land, whereupon the 
maintenance of special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other 
provisions of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner. 
 
13. This Special Use Permit and the subject site shall be reviewed and inspected by Planning and 
Development Staff on the fifth (5 th) anniversary of Board of Supervisors approval and every five (5)

Great Sky Camp Ranch 
On-site Water and Wastewater Systems 
Design Report 
Introduction 
The purpose of this report is to describe the water and on-site  wastewater systems 
planned for the new RV spaces that will be constructed.  The existing septic system for the 
existing building will remain in service.  The existing well wi ll be connected to a new 
storage tank and booster station to provide water for the RV spaces. 
 
Existing Conditions 
There is one existing onsite wastewater system at the site that  will remain in service.  It 
serves the existing building and two existing RV spaces and has  a 2000-gallon septic tank 
and 900 gal/day capacity.   
 
The existing well was drilled in 2018 by the previous owner and  the ADWR well record 
shows it was drilled 420 feet deep with the static water level at 360 feet below the surface.  
The record is included in the Appendix. 
 
 
Setbacks and Limiting Conditions 
The setbacks for the wastewater system are 100 ft from the well , 50 feet from the property 
lines for vacant lots (parcel to the SW), 5 ft from water service lines, 10 feet from buildings, 5 
feet from utilities and easements, and 5 feet from walls, drive way and parking areas. The 
overall slope of the site is 1-2 percent down to the north. 
 
Design Water and Wastewater Flow 
The new systems will provide wastewater service for 63 RV space s.  The demand and 
design flows for the systems will be 6300 gallons per day based  on 100 gpd/RV space. The 
wastewater will be entirely residential in nature. The system w ill be constructed to serve the 
new spaces after approval in late 2023 and early 2024. 
 
The total flow for the entire site for the existing system and new system will be 7200 gpd. 
 Total Design Flow: 900 gpd existing septic system + 6300 gpd n ew septic system 
= 7200 gpd 
 
The size of the site is 10.00 acres.  Nitrogen removal will be required by the wastewater 
system to reduce the nitrogen loading under the limit of 39.9 g /ac/day.  The calculations are 
included in the Appendix. 
 
The peak water demand, assuming 63 RV hookups, is projected to be 252 gpm, assuming 8 
plumbing fixture per RV and 4 gpm peak demand for each RV.  The  peak hour demand is 
projected to be 2500 gallons assuming the daily demand occurs over a 3 hour period.

<!-- page 1262 -->
Mills Engineering LLC 
      water & wastewater system design 
 
 3
On-Site Wastewater Site Investigation 
The site investigation was performed and results showed the soi l texture was Sandy Clay 
Loam with SAR of 0.40 gpd/sf. 
 
Design Criteria 
Sewerlines 
The RV spaces will have hookups with 3-inch to 4-inch diameter SDR 35 PVC or 
DWV with cleanouts for maintenance of the lines.  The pipes will be sloped as 
required by the plumbing code at a minimum of 1/8-inch per foot with a minimum of 
18 inches of cover.  The pipes will drain by gravity to the wastewater system. 
 
Water System 
Each space will also have a water service connection for the RV with frost free 
connection.  The water and sewer lines will be separated as required by the 
plumbing code.  The well will be tested for Safe Drinking Water parameters for the 
new source approval.  The well will pump the water into a new 10,000 gallon storage 
tank and a booster pump will provide 40-60 psi pressure to the pipes to the RV 
space.  Materials and equipment will meet the standards for safe drinking water.  
The water system will be permitted as a transient non-community water system 
serving more than 25 people. 
 
Wastewater Treatment 
Textile Filter Treatment System 
The sewer collection pipes will be connected to solids settling tank and then flow to a 
recirculation tank that will have pumps to dose textile filters and recycle the 
wastewater.  The first tank will provide quiescent conditions to allow solids to settle 
and be removed from the wastewater.  It is sized for at least 2.1 days of storage. 
 
Solids Settling Tank: 6300 gpd(2.1)=13,230 gallons – use 15,000 gal tank 
Recirculation/Dosing Tank: 6300 gallons required – use 7,000 gal tank 
 
 
The site limitations require treatment to lower the nitrogen, bacteria, Biochemical 
Oxygen Demand (BOD
5) and Total Suspended Solids (TSS) of the wastewater.  
Textile filter treatment with an Aerocell Treatment system was chosen to meet the 
nitrogen loading limit.  The units are manufactured by: 
Quanics by ANUA 
Anua International LLC 
4106 Bernau Avenue 
Greensboro, North Carolina 27407 
336.547.9338 
https://quanics.net/aerocell%2Fbiocoir

<!-- page 1263 -->
Mills Engineering LLC 
      water & wastewater system design 
 
 4
Each of the modules provides 1500 gal/day of treatment capacity and six will be 
provided.  The system is NSF approved, and listed on the ADEQ approved 
proprietary product list.  It is designed for a 20-year operational life. The system will 
treat the effluent below 3 and 2 mg/l BOD5 and TSS.  The preliminary plan in the 
Appendix shows the location of the treatment system. 
 
The textile filter units will provide treatment and split the flow so 20% is discharged 
to the trenches and 80% is recycled back to the first tank.  For the Aerocell units, the 
wastewater is pumped to the filter modules where the media provides a surface for 
microorganisms to grow and remove contaminants from the wastewater.  There is a 
vent fan to keep the filters with oxygen for transfers to allow aerobic organisms fixed 
to the media to grow and use the organics as food.   
 
The installation will follow the requirements of AAC R18-9-E312 for textile filter 
systems with subsurface disposal and the manufacturer’s instructions.    
 
Disposal 
Rock Trenches 
Following treatment, the effluent will be pumped to trenches to dispersal in the soil.   
 
Final Grading 
The final site grading after installation of the tanks and trenches will include installing 
a swale or berm to divert runoff around the system, compacted to 85%. 
 
Controls 
The treatment system will have a visible and audible alarm will  be located on the 
control in a visible location as required by AAC R18-9-E304.   
 
Reserve Area 
The reserve area is shown on the east side of the RV spaced for future trenches.

I. INTRODUCTION 
 
The Greatsky Campranch project is located in Navajo County, near Show Low, 
Arizona at 7863 White Mountain Lake Road. The site is located on parcel number 
304-22-005 which is 10.00 acres in size. The site currently has one 3600 square 
foot commercial building and a few sheds and storage buildings. The proposed 
improvements to the site include an RV park with 63 proposed RV spaces. New 
gravel roads will be constructed to access these RV spaces. 
  
The purpose of this report is to provide the results of the preliminary drainage 
analysis that was performed, estimating the anticipated flows for the 2-year, 10-
year, 50-year and 100-year storm events for the proposed conditions and provide 
calculations for handling these flows.  
 
 
 
 
Figure 1. Vicinity Map 
 
 
II. METHODOLOGY 
 
The analysis methodology was based on the rational method, shown in Equation 1 below. 
The rational method was used to estimate peak flow rates for the storm events. 
Runoff coefficients for the site were determined using the ADOT Highway 
Drainage Design Manual-Volume 2. 
SITE

<!-- page 1294 -->
Page 2 
 
 
Equation 1. The Rational Method 
 
Q=C*I*A 
 
Q= Peak Flow Rate (cfs) 
C= Runoff Coefficient (C) 
I= Rainfall Intensity (inches per hour) 
A= Area (Acres) 
 
The peak flow rates were estimated using the AutoCAD Civil 3D “Hydraflow 
Hydrographs Extension” to route the flows through the site and to estimate the 
peak flows for the 2-year, 10-year, 50-year and 100-year events at specific 
concentration points. Rainfall data was determined using the NOAA Atlas 14 
website for Atlas 14, Volume 1, Version 5 near the project site.  
 
Autodesk’s Hydraflow Hydrographs Extension was used to create hydrographs. 
Hydrographs were then used to route flows through the site.  
 
The analysis developed flow rates for the pre and post flow rates for the 2, 10, 50 
and 100-year events for the project.  
 
The drainage area was delineated from recent mapping for the site and from field 
observations.  
 
 
III. EXISTING CONDITIONS 
 
The site is located at the southeast corner of the intersection of White Mountain 
Lake Road and Woodside Trail. The site generally drains in a northeasterly 
direction towards two 18-inch culverts that drain to the north under White Mountain 
Lake Road. Figure 2 shows how the existing drainage flows across the site with 
flow arrows placed perpendicular to the existing contours. 
 
An existing drainage area across the property was analyzed with the outfall being 
the two existing culverts near the northeast corner of the property. Topographic 
mapping from the National Geodetic Survey (NGS) website was used to delineate 
the drainage area that included the site. This drainage area and the outflow 
location is shown in Figure 4 in the appendix. 
 
A weighted runoff coefficient “C” was determined for the existing site. To 
determine the weighted runoff coefficient, each area with a different surface 
material was assigned a C-value. It was determined that a C-value of 0.55 would 
be used for the areas with native grasses and juniper trees, 0.78 was used for the 
areas of existing gravel or cinder roads/driveways, and 0.98 was used for any 
impervious surfaces. These weighted C-value calculations are shown in the table 
on page A-4 in the appendix.

<!-- page 1295 -->
Page 3 
 
 
Due to the size of the drainage areas that were analyzed, the minimum time of 
concentration of 10 minutes was used for this analysis. 
 
The existing peak flows leaving the site were determined and are shown below. 
 
• 2-year = 205.7 cfs 
• 10-year = 326.9 cfs 
• 50-year = 457.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 520.2 cfs 
 
Figure 2. Existing Site 
 
 
IV. PROPOSED CONDITIONS 
 
The proposed improvements to the site include construction of 63 RV spaces. 
Each space will have a level gravel area to park the RV and at least two vehicles. 
vehicles. Figure 3 in the Appendix shows the proposed layout for the 
improvements to the site. 
 
Site

<!-- page 1296 -->
Page 4 
 
A weighted runoff coefficient “C” was determined for the post-development 
drainage from the site. To determine the weighted runoff coefficient, the same C-
values used for the existing drainage were again used and the area for each 
surface were adjusted to account for the additional impervious surface. These 
weighted C-value calculations are shown in the table on page A-4 in the appendix. 
  
For the proposed site analysis, two drainage areas were analyzed. One drainage 
area consists of everything that will go to the detention basin before reaching the 
outfall point and the other drainage area is everything that will not go through the 
detention basin but still make it to the outfall point. These drainage areas are 
shown in Figure 5 in the appendix. Drainage swales shall be utilized along the 
South and East sides of the property to direct most of the offsite flows around the 
site and directly to the outflow point. For this analysis the minimum time of 
concentration of 10 minutes was also used. 
 
Post-development drainage area A (direct to outfall) 
• 2-year = 183.7 cfs 
• 10-year = 291.9 cfs 
• 50-year = 408.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 464.5 cfs 
Post-development drainage area B (to detention basin) 
• 2-year = 27.4 cfs 
• 10-year = 43.6 cfs 
• 50-year = 61.0 cfs 
• 100-year = 69.3 cfs 
The proposed detention basin will be located on the north side of the site, near 
White Mountain Lake Road, and catch the storm water runoff coming from 
drainage area B. The bottom elevation of the detention basin shall be 6061.50 
feet, and the top of the basin shall be 6063.50 feet. The total available storage in 
the detention basin shall be 13,463 cubic feet. The basin shall outlet through two 
12-inch culverts and two 18-inch culverts at the east end of the basin. The basin 
will also have a 30-foot rip rap weir at an elevation of 6063.00 feet. 
 
Utilizing the detention basin, the proposed flows from drainage area B were 
reduced to the numbers estimated below:  
 
• 2-year = 13.8 cfs 
• 10-year = 31.8 cfs

<!-- page 1297 -->
Page 5 
 
• 50-year = 50.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 58.8 cfs 
The reduced values from drainage area B after passing through the detention 
basin were added together with the flows from drainage area A and the total post-
development flows to the outfall were calculated. The sum of those flows is shown 
below: 
 
• 2-year = 195.2 cfs 
• 10-year = 310.5 cfs 
• 50-year = 450.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 516.1 cfs 
When the existing flows are compared to the proposed flows after the detention 
basin, it can be seen that the total flows from the property will effectively be 
decreased.  
 
VI. SUMMARY 
 
The construction of the proposed RV park at 7863 White Mountain Lake Road will 
cause an increase in storm water runoff from the site. A detention basin will be 
constructed to mitigate the increase in on-site stormwater runoff flows. As 
demonstrated, the project will result in an overall decreased rate of stormwater 
runoff from the site.

 2
 
Great Sky Camp Ranch 
On-site Water and Wastewater Systems 
Design Report 
Introduction 
The purpose of this report is to describe the water and on-site  wastewater systems 
planned for the new RV spaces that will be constructed.  The existing septic system for the 
existing building will remain in service.  The existing well wi ll be connected to a new 
storage tank and booster station to provide water for the RV spaces. 
 
Existing Conditions 
There is one existing onsite wastewater system at the site that  will remain in service.  It 
serves the existing building and two existing RV spaces and has  a 2000-gallon septic tank 
and 900 gal/day capacity.   
 
The existing well was drilled in 2018 by the previous owner and  the ADWR well record 
shows it was drilled 420 feet deep with the static water level at 360 feet below the surface.  
The record is included in the Appendix. 
 
 
Setbacks and Limiting Conditions 
The setbacks for the wastewater system are 100 ft from the well , 50 feet from the property 
lines for vacant lots (parcel to the SW), 5 ft from water service lines, 10 feet from buildings, 5 
feet from utilities and easements, and 5 feet from walls, drive way and parking areas. The 
overall slope of the site is 1-2 percent down to the north. 
 
Design Water and Wastewater Flow 
The new systems will provide wastewater service for 63 RV space s.  The demand and 
design flows for the systems will be 6300 gallons per day based  on 100 gpd/RV space. The 
wastewater will be entirely residential in nature. The system w ill be constructed to serve the 
new spaces after approval in late 2023 and early 2024. 
 
The total flow for the entire site for the existing system and new system will be 7200 gpd. 
 Total Design Flow: 900 gpd existing septic system + 6300 gpd n ew septic system 
= 7200 gpd 
 
The size of the site is 10.00 acres.  Nitrogen removal will be required by the wastewater 
system to reduce the nitrogen loading under the limit of 39.9 g /ac/day.  The calculations are 
included in the Appendix. 
 
The peak water demand, assuming 63 RV hookups, is projected to be 252 gpm, assuming 8 
plumbing fixture per RV and 4 gpm peak demand for each RV.  The  peak hour demand is 
projected to be 2500 gallons assuming the daily demand occurs over a 3 hour period.

<!-- page 1317 -->
Mills Engineering LLC 
      water & wastewater system design 
 
 3
On-Site Wastewater Site Investigation 
The site investigation was performed and results showed the soi l texture was Sandy Clay 
Loam with SAR of 0.40 gpd/sf. 
 
Design Criteria 
Sewerlines 
The RV spaces will have hookups with 3-inch to 4-inch diameter SDR 35 PVC or 
DWV with cleanouts for maintenance of the lines.  The pipes will be sloped as 
required by the plumbing code at a minimum of 1/8-inch per foot with a minimum of 
18 inches of cover.  The pipes will drain by gravity to the wastewater system. 
 
Water System 
Each space will also have a water service connection for the RV with frost free 
connection.  The water and sewer lines will be separated as required by the 
plumbing code.  The well will be tested for Safe Drinking Water parameters for the 
new source approval.  The well will pump the water into a new 10,000 gallon storage 
tank and a booster pump will provide 40-60 psi pressure to the pipes to the RV 
space.  Materials and equipment will meet the standards for safe drinking water.  
The water system will be permitted as a transient non-community water system 
serving more than 25 people. 
 
Wastewater Treatment 
Textile Filter Treatment System 
The sewer collection pipes will be connected to solids settling tank and then flow to a 
recirculation tank that will have pumps to dose textile filters and recycle the 
wastewater.  The first tank will provide quiescent conditions to allow solids to settle 
and be removed from the wastewater.  It is sized for at least 2.1 days of storage. 
 
Solids Settling Tank: 6300 gpd(2.1)=13,230 gallons – use 15,000 gal tank 
Recirculation/Dosing Tank: 6300 gallons required – use 7,000 gal tank 
 
 
The site limitations require treatment to lower the nitrogen, bacteria, Biochemical 
Oxygen Demand (BOD
5) and Total Suspended Solids (TSS) of the wastewater.  
Textile filter treatment with an Aerocell Treatment system was chosen to meet the 
nitrogen loading limit.  The units are manufactured by: 
Quanics by ANUA 
Anua International LLC 
4106 Bernau Avenue 
Greensboro, North Carolina 27407 
336.547.9338 
https://quanics.net/aerocell%2Fbiocoir

<!-- page 1318 -->
Mills Engineering LLC 
      water & wastewater system design 
 
 4
Each of the modules provides 1500 gal/day of treatment capacity and six will be 
provided.  The system is NSF approved, and listed on the ADEQ approved 
proprietary product list.  It is designed for a 20-year operational life. The system will 
treat the effluent below 3 and 2 mg/l BOD5 and TSS.  The preliminary plan in the 
Appendix shows the location of the treatment system. 
 
The textile filter units will provide treatment and split the flow so 20% is discharged 
to the trenches and 80% is recycled back to the first tank.  For the Aerocell units, the 
wastewater is pumped to the filter modules where the media provides a surface for 
microorganisms to grow and remove contaminants from the wastewater.  There is a 
vent fan to keep the filters with oxygen for transfers to allow aerobic organisms fixed 
to the media to grow and use the organics as food.   
 
The installation will follow the requirements of AAC R18-9-E312 for textile filter 
systems with subsurface disposal and the manufacturer’s instructions.    
 
Disposal 
Rock Trenches 
Following treatment, the effluent will be pumped to trenches to dispersal in the soil.   
 
Final Grading 
The final site grading after installation of the tanks and trenches will include installing 
a swale or berm to divert runoff around the system, compacted to 85%. 
 
Controls 
The treatment system will have a visible and audible alarm will  be located on the 
control in a visible location as required by AAC R18-9-E304.   
 
Reserve Area 
The reserve area is shown on the east side of the RV spaced for future trenches.

I. INTRODUCTION 
 
The Greatsky Campranch project is located in Navajo County, near Show Low, 
Arizona at 7863 White Mountain Lake Road. The site is located on parcel number 
304-22-005 which is 10.00 acres in size. The site currently has one 3600 square 
foot commercial building and a few sheds and storage buildings. The proposed 
improvements to the site include an RV park with 63 proposed RV spaces. New 
gravel roads will be constructed to access these RV spaces. 
  
The purpose of this report is to provide the results of the preliminary drainage 
analysis that was performed, estimating the anticipated flows for the 2-year, 10-
year, 50-year and 100-year storm events for the proposed conditions and provide 
calculations for handling these flows.  
 
 
 
 
Figure 1. Vicinity Map 
 
 
II. METHODOLOGY 
 
The analysis methodology was based on the rational method, shown in Equation 1 below. 
The rational method was used to estimate peak flow rates for the storm events. 
Runoff coefficients for the site were determined using the ADOT Highway 
Drainage Design Manual-Volume 2. 
SITE

<!-- page 1342 -->
Page 2 
 
 
Equation 1. The Rational Method 
 
Q=C*I*A 
 
Q= Peak Flow Rate (cfs) 
C= Runoff Coefficient (C) 
I= Rainfall Intensity (inches per hour) 
A= Area (Acres) 
 
The peak flow rates were estimated using the AutoCAD Civil 3D “Hydraflow 
Hydrographs Extension” to route the flows through the site and to estimate the 
peak flows for the 2-year, 10-year, 50-year and 100-year events at specific 
concentration points. Rainfall data was determined using the NOAA Atlas 14 
website for Atlas 14, Volume 1, Version 5 near the project site.  
 
Autodesk’s Hydraflow Hydrographs Extension was used to create hydrographs. 
Hydrographs were then used to route flows through the site.  
 
The analysis developed flow rates for the pre and post flow rates for the 2, 10, 50 
and 100-year events for the project.  
 
The drainage area was delineated from recent mapping for the site and from field 
observations.  
 
 
III. EXISTING CONDITIONS 
 
The site is located at the southeast corner of the intersection of White Mountain 
Lake Road and Woodside Trail. The site generally drains in a northeasterly 
direction towards two 18-inch culverts that drain to the north under White Mountain 
Lake Road. Figure 2 shows how the existing drainage flows across the site with 
flow arrows placed perpendicular to the existing contours. 
 
An existing drainage area across the property was analyzed with the outfall being 
the two existing culverts near the northeast corner of the property. Topographic 
mapping from the National Geodetic Survey (NGS) website was used to delineate 
the drainage area that included the site. This drainage area and the outflow 
location is shown in Figure 4 in the appendix. 
 
A weighted runoff coefficient “C” was determined for the existing site. To 
determine the weighted runoff coefficient, each area with a different surface 
material was assigned a C-value. It was determined that a C-value of 0.55 would 
be used for the areas with native grasses and juniper trees, 0.78 was used for the 
areas of existing gravel or cinder roads/driveways, and 0.98 was used for any 
impervious surfaces. These weighted C-value calculations are shown in the table 
on page A-4 in the appendix.

<!-- page 1343 -->
Page 3 
 
 
Due to the size of the drainage areas that were analyzed, the minimum time of 
concentration of 10 minutes was used for this analysis. 
 
The existing peak flows leaving the site were determined and are shown below. 
 
• 2-year = 205.7 cfs 
• 10-year = 326.9 cfs 
• 50-year = 457.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 520.2 cfs 
 
Figure 2. Existing Site 
 
 
IV. PROPOSED CONDITIONS 
 
The proposed improvements to the site include construction of 63 RV spaces. 
Each space will have a level gravel area to park the RV and at least two vehicles. 
vehicles. Figure 3 in the Appendix shows the proposed layout for the 
improvements to the site. 
 
Site

<!-- page 1344 -->
Page 4 
 
A weighted runoff coefficient “C” was determined for the post-development 
drainage from the site. To determine the weighted runoff coefficient, the same C-
values used for the existing drainage were again used and the area for each 
surface were adjusted to account for the additional impervious surface. These 
weighted C-value calculations are shown in the table on page A-4 in the appendix. 
  
For the proposed site analysis, two drainage areas were analyzed. One drainage 
area consists of everything that will go to the detention basin before reaching the 
outfall point and the other drainage area is everything that will not go through the 
detention basin but still make it to the outfall point. These drainage areas are 
shown in Figure 5 in the appendix. Drainage swales shall be utilized along the 
South and East sides of the property to direct most of the offsite flows around the 
site and directly to the outflow point. For this analysis the minimum time of 
concentration of 10 minutes was also used. 
 
Post-development drainage area A (direct to outfall) 
• 2-year = 183.7 cfs 
• 10-year = 291.9 cfs 
• 50-year = 408.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 464.5 cfs 
Post-development drainage area B (to detention basin) 
• 2-year = 27.4 cfs 
• 10-year = 43.6 cfs 
• 50-year = 61.0 cfs 
• 100-year = 69.3 cfs 
The proposed detention basin will be located on the north side of the site, near 
White Mountain Lake Road, and catch the storm water runoff coming from 
drainage area B. The bottom elevation of the detention basin shall be 6061.50 
feet, and the top of the basin shall be 6063.50 feet. The total available storage in 
the detention basin shall be 13,463 cubic feet. The basin shall outlet through two 
12-inch culverts and two 18-inch culverts at the east end of the basin. The basin 
will also have a 30-foot rip rap weir at an elevation of 6063.00 feet. 
 
Utilizing the detention basin, the proposed flows from drainage area B were 
reduced to the numbers estimated below:  
 
• 2-year = 13.8 cfs 
• 10-year = 31.8 cfs

<!-- page 1345 -->
Page 5 
 
• 50-year = 50.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 58.8 cfs 
The reduced values from drainage area B after passing through the detention 
basin were added together with the flows from drainage area A and the total post-
development flows to the outfall were calculated. The sum of those flows is shown 
below: 
 
• 2-year = 195.2 cfs 
• 10-year = 310.5 cfs 
• 50-year = 450.7 cfs 
• 100-year = 516.1 cfs 
When the existing flows are compared to the proposed flows after the detention 
basin, it can be seen that the total flows from the property will effectively be 
decreased.  
 
VI. SUMMARY 
 
The construction of the proposed RV park at 7863 White Mountain Lake Road will 
cause an increase in storm water runoff from the site. A detention basin will be 
constructed to mitigate the increase in on-site stormwater runoff flows. As 
demonstrated, the project will result in an overall decreased rate of stormwater 
runoff from the site.

Location: The property is located in the White Mountain Lakes area on APN # 304-22-005. 
 
Size: 10.00 acres 
 
Supervisor District: III 
 
Zoning: C-R (Commercial-Residential Zoning District) 
 
Property Owners: FSBC Properties LLC 
 
Applicant: Michael and Courtney Barclay 
 
Representative: Emery Ellsworth 
 
REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
A request for a Special Use Permit to  allow for construction of a 63 space RV Park on a 10.00 -acre 
parcel, in the White Mountain Lakes area. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
To the west of the subject property is a mini -storage facility.  To the south of this property are single -
family residential properties.  To the east of this property is a kennel and animal crematorium.  To the 
north of this property is White Mountain Lake Road and single-family residential properties. 
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY:

<!-- page 1362 -->
Board of Supervisors              2 | P a g e  
 
 
In the past, the subject property had been utilized for community swap meets , as a dance hall, and for 
community gatherings. 
 
Currently on-site, there is a craft brewery with a tap house and music venue.  The applicant has noted 
that the property is intended to be occasionally utilized as a wedding center. 
 
On the property, there are already commercial buildings, bathrooms, a music stage, a water well, and a 
2000-gallon septic system. 
 
At the Thursday, October 19 th, 2023 Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing, the Navajo County 
Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended approval of this Special Use Permit, 
subject to the conditions recommended by Staff. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The proposed project will have the following: 
 
▪ 63 RV Spaces 
▪ Solid fencing, surrounding the property, between 3 and ½ feet and 6 feet in height  
▪ A private driveway 
▪ Open, undeveloped area 
▪ A water well and private water system 
▪ A 15,000-gallon solids settling tank and 7,000 -gallon recirculating/dosing tank, for on-
site wastewater treatment 
▪ A Knox Box, per Timber-Mesa Fire and Medical District 
▪ A bath house 
▪ Propane 
▪ Satellite internet 
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
ARTICLE 15 – (C-R) COMMERCIAL-RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
Section 1501 – Purpose.  
 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for shops and services in convenient 
locations to meet the daily needs of families in the immediate residential neighborhoods and 
wholesaling or distribution activities in locations where there is adequate access to major streets 
or highways.  Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include retail and wholesale 
commerce, commercial entertainment, and some uses of a light manufacturing nature. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses

The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
29. Recreation Vehicle Parks, subject to all the regulations applicable to RV parks, 
specified in the use regulations for the “R-3’ zoning district.

PLANNING AND ZONING COMMISSION/STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended approval of this Special 
Use Permit, subject to the conditions recommended by Staff. 
 
Navajo County Planning and Development Services Staff recommend approval of the Special Use Permit,  
subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. The applicant shall obtain any required Navajo County permits, including, but not limited to 
building, sewer connection, grading, drainage, and sign permits. 
 
2. All corners shall be according to vision triangle rules and regulations.  No building or fencing 
shall obstruct the view of traffic. 
 
3. No building or structure shall be occupied prior to complete compliance with all appropriate 
Building Division requirements. 
 
4. All lighting on the property shall be shielded to reflect downward, be motion -activated, and be 
in conformance with the Navajo County Lighting Ordinance. 
 
5. A Site Lighting Plan, prepared by an Electrical Engineer, licensed in the State of Arizona 
(required by code for commercial projects), shall be submitted and approved. 
 
6. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan.  Any 
expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this Permit. 
 
7. A fence, of material acceptable to the Planning and Development Services Director, shall be 
constructed around the boundary of the property. 
 
8. A Geotechnical Report for access to, and within, the property shall be submitted and approved. 
 
9. A Grading and Drainage Plan shall be submitted and approved. 
 
10. A Drainage Study, which meets the Navajo County Drainage Policy, shall be submitted and 
approved. 
 
11. A water system design, meeting the requirements of the Timber-Mesa Fire and Medical District, 
shall be submitted and approved. 
 
12. The applicant shall connect to an existing water system or create a new water system, which is 
approved by ADEQ, to supply drinking water to the development. 
 
13. The applicant shall connect to a wastewater system or create a new wastewater treatment system,

<!-- page 1368 -->
Board of Supervisors              8 | P a g e  
 
which is approved by ADEQ, to treat and dispose of wastewater from the development. 
 
14. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period, from the date of 
Board approval, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
15. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the specific use and 
to the specific property for which it is issued. Upon completion and final inspection by the Planning 
and Development Services Director (or designee) of any authorized structures, signifying that all 
zoning and site development requirements imposed in connection with the permit have been satisfied, 
the Special Use Permit shall thereafter be transferable and shall run with the land, whereupon the 
maintenance of special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other 
provisions of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner. 
 
16. This Special Use Permit and the subject site shall be reviewed and inspected by Planning and 
Development Staff on the fifth (5 th) anniversary of Board of Supervisors approval and every five (5) 
years thereafter to ensure the site is being utilized as approved and is in compliance with all conditions 
contained herein.  If the subject site is found to be out of compliance with these conditions, this Special 
Use Permit and its privileges may be revoked.

Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 48-2023,
approving/denying the construction and operation of a 1,000 MW solar power generation
facility, 1,000 MW Battery Energy Storage System, and associated facilities on approximately

Background:
The subject parcels for this project are vacant, and have historically been used for grazing land,
and other associated ranching activities. The land is currently owned by W.B. Jeffers Jr., Louis
A. Jeffers, Ann E. Jeffers, and the Jeffers Cattle Co. The applicant has indicated they have
entered into a Land Purchase and Sale Option Agreement with the owners of the subject parcels,
and once exercised, Snowflake Solar LLC. will retain complete ownership of the parcels.
Snowflake Solar LLC. has also entered into a Large Generator Interconnection Agreement with
Arizona Public Service (APS), assuring access to the APS transmission system upon
completion of the gen-tie line.  
During their October 19th, 2023, meeting, the Navajo County Planning and Zoning
Commission recommended approval of the Special Use Permit, including all conditions as
recommended by Staff within the Staff Report.
 
Recommendation: 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission and Navajo County Planning and
Development Staff recommend approval of the Special Use Permit, subject to the conditions
within the Staff Report.
